subject: Post-call: model fit + Redwood-verified benchmarks & next steps
messages:
From: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme-retail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-21T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + next steps (model fit & benchmarks)

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Goal: evaluate viable models for Acme's instant-recommendations use case (short product descriptions + user context) while meeting 99th pctile latency <= 120ms and sustaining 200 TPS during peak batches.
- Primary concerns you mentioned: output quality consistency on custom prompts, inference cost at scale, and ability to detect quality regressions after model updates.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll share Redwood-verified benchmark links for candidate models + a short summary (TPS, latency p50/p95/p99).
2) SE-run eval using your prompt set (you mentioned ~1.2k prompts) — Marissa will coordinate for access.
3) If model candidates look good, run a 72-hour canary on Dedicated with auto-fallback to a lower-cost variant.

I’ve attached a short benchmark summary and the Redwood performance profiles. Marissa, can you pick this up and schedule the eval run once Sofia sends the prompt set?

Sofia — can you share the prompt set and a sample of the telemetry you’d like to preserve (latency/cost/labels)? If you’d prefer, drop links to the Drive folder and we’ll pull from there.

Thanks — talk soon.

Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference runtime

Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps (model fit & benchmarks)

Thanks Alex — this looks good. Couple quick items: 

- I attached the prompt set (acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) and a small CSV of production latency samples.
- We currently target p95 < 90ms in production, but we can accept p99 up to 120ms for background recommendations. For the instant-reco surface, p99 should be <= 110ms ideally.
- We do want automatic regression alerts — ideally tied to a stable eval set and thresholded on generation quality. Can your platform surface BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics or do you recommend custom evals?

Marissa — looping you in to help define the eval config and any additional telemetry fields we should share.

Sofia
Director of Product, Acme Retail
sofia.ramos@acme-retail.com
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme-retail.com>
Cc: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps (model fit & benchmarks)

Hi Sofia — thanks for the prompt set and latency sample. I pulled together Redwood-verified performance profiles for the candidate models we discussed on the call. Summary below + links (full CSV attached).

High-level recommended candidates (ordered by quality -> cost):
- redwood-xl-rlhf-2026 (best quality, quant-friendly)
  - Measured at 200 TPS sustained (batched), p50=24ms, p95=75ms, p99=110ms, avg tokens/sec per GPU consistent with your average sequence lengths.
- gpt-open-13b-quant (cost-efficient but slightly lower tail latency)
  - Measured 200 TPS (batching), p50=28ms, p95=88ms, p99=130ms — meets p95 target, p99 slightly above your strict instant-reco p99.
- redwood-medium-quant (fallback variant, low-cost)
  - Good for background recommendations; p95=120ms, p99=180ms, much lower per-token cost.

Benchmarks & artifacts shared:
- Redwood performance profiles (attached: redwood_performance_profiles.csv) — includes kernel selection, sequence length distribution used, and hardware profile.
- Public benchmark view: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-2026-07 (access granted to your email).
- Eval harness: I kicked off a seeded run on your prompt set with basic quality metrics (token overlap + pairwise human eval sampling). Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example

Notes on quality/regression monitoring:
- We recommend a two-tier approach: (1) automated metrics on your stable eval set (BLEU-style and semantic similarity with embeddings) with thresholds that trigger alerts, and (2) periodic human sampling for prompts that show high metric variance.
- Redwood Optimize can run daily evals and file a regression alert if metric delta > X% over a 7-day moving window (we can tune X; suggested default 3–5%).

Next steps (action items):
- Sofia: confirm acceptance of the three candidates to proceed with a 72-hour canary on Dedicated (we’ll provision a small reserved pool).
- Alex: provide pricing estimates for the canary (including expected token cost delta for quantized vs non-quantized).
- Marissa/Dylan: we’ll schedule the eval run and set up regression alerts; I’ll share the results in ~48 hours.

Attachments: redwood_performance_profiles.csv, acme_benchmark_summary.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps (model fit & benchmarks)

Thanks all — quick follow: pricing and next scheduling items.

Pricing snapshot for 72-hour canary (estimated):
- redwood-xl-rlhf-2026 (non-quant): ~$7,200 total (includes reserved GPU time + tokens) — high quality, lowest regression risk.
- gpt-open-13b-quant: ~$3,400 total — good middle ground; recommend extra sampling to validate p99 behavior on your heaviest prompts.
- redwood-medium-quant (fallback): ~$900 — intended as fallback only.

Sofia — if you approve, we’ll:
1) Provision Dedicated canary capacity for the selected model (we’ll keep autoscale off for the canary).
2) Run the 72-hour eval with daily regression alerts; Marissa will share daily summaries and the final report.
3) After canary, we can propose a rollout plan with gradual traffic ramp over 7–14 days and automatic fallback policies to the medium-quant variant.

Please reply with which candidate you want to canary, and any additional telemetry fields you want included in the regression alerts (e.g., session_id, request_size, user_segment).

Thanks — Alex
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
